info.title: AKIRA Ops Suite API
info.description:
Internal multi-outlet restaurant operations platform.

Authenticate with a Supabase access token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

get.description:
Profile, global role and outlet memberships for the current session.

The client uses this to decide which shell to render, so it is the first
call after sign-in.

patch.description:
Change your own name or phone. Role, outlets and activation are not
editable here — those are administrative actions.

get.description:
What the signed-in user may grant, plus a plain-language reason for each
role they may not. The UI disables the rest with the reason attached rather
than omitting them — a rule you cannot see is a rule you will argue with.

Owners and operations managers see everyone. An outlet manager sees only
people in their own outlets.

post.description:
Supabase sends the invitation and owns the token, so no password is ever
handled here.

You can never grant a role at or above your own. An existing address is not
an error: that person keeps the login they already have.

patch.description:
Deactivating the last active owner is refused: it would lock everyone out
of outlet and user administration permanently.

put.description: Outlet roles follow the global role, so the two cannot silently disagree.
Replaces the whole set. The first outlet becomes their primary.

put.summary: Set or clear a shared-tablet PIN
put.description:
A PIN attributes floor work on a shared tablet to a real person. It
authorises floor actions only, can never approve a run, and is only accepted
on a device already bound to that person's outlet.

Sending `null` clears it, which is how a departing staff member comes off
the tablet without losing their history. Only shift leads and staff may
have one.

get.description:
Owners and operations managers see every outlet. Everyone else sees only
the outlets they belong to.

parameters.name: include_inactive

schema.description: Include outlets that have been deactivated.
schema.title: Include Inactive

parameters.description: Include outlets that have been deactivated.

post.description: Owner only. The code must be unique and is fixed once created.

patch.description:
Owner only. Changes only the fields present in the body. The code cannot
be changed — it appears in exports and printed sheets.

delete.description:
Owner only. A soft delete: history is kept, the outlet stops appearing.

Refused with 409 while any checklist run is still pending, in progress or
awaiting review — closing the outlet under them would strand work someone
is in the middle of.

post.description:
Owner only. Binds an existing Supabase auth account to one outlet.

The account itself is created out of band, so this API never mints or
transports a credential.

delete.description:
Owner only. Use this the moment a tablet goes missing: it stops that
account reaching any outlet data, without touching the runs it already
recorded.

get.description: Liveness probe. Must never touch the database.

Readiness probe. Unlike /healthz this does check the database, because a
process that cannot reach Postgres is running but not serving.

DeviceSummary.title: DeviceSummary
DeviceSummary.description: Present only when the caller is a shared outlet tablet.

GrantableRolesResponse.title: GrantableRolesResponse
GrantableRolesResponse.description:
What the signed-in user may assign, so the UI can disable the rest with
an explanation instead of hiding it.

SetOutletsRequest.title: SetOutletsRequest
SetOutletsRequest.description:
Replaces the whole membership set, rather than adding to it.

A replace makes the resulting state obvious from the request. An add/remove
pair leaves the caller guessing what the person ended up with.

UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest
UpdateMeRequest.description:
Only what a person may change about themselves.

Role, outlets and activation are deliberately absent: allowing them here
would let anyone promote themselves through their own profile.

UpdateOutletRequest.title: UpdateOutletRequest
UpdateOutletRequest.description:
Every field optional: a PATCH changes only what it names.

`code` is absent on purpose. It appears in exports, conversation and
printed sheets, so renaming it silently would break references nobody is
tracking.
